name: Decisional Balance
description: Evaluating pros and cons of options to clarify preferences and consequences.
creator: Janet Bavelas
core_principles: Structured comparison of benefits and costs across choices.

name: Six Thinking Hats
description: Parallel thinking framework using six perspectives to explore a topic.
creator: Edward de Bono
core_principles: Segregate thinking modes to reduce conflict and broaden insight.

name: Root Cause Analysis
description: Technique focused on identifying the underlying cause of a problem.
creator: Sakichi Toyoda
core_principles: Five Whys questioning and causal mapping to reach the root issue.

name: SMART Goals
description: Goal-setting framework ensuring objectives are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound.
creator: George T. Doran
core_principles: Structured criteria enhance clarity and accountability.

name: SWOT Analysis
description: Assessing Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats for strategic decisions.
creator: Albert Humphrey
core_principles: Holistic situational awareness to guide action.

name: Gibbs Reflective Cycle
description: Six-stage reflective learning cycle: Description, Feelings, Evaluation, Analysis, Conclusion, and Action Plan.
creator: Graham Gibbs
core_principles: Combine descriptive recall, emotional awareness, and analysis to generate conclusions and plan improvements.

name: GROW Model
description: Coaching framework: Goal, Reality, Options, Way Forward to structure progress-oriented conversations.
creator: John Whitmore
core_principles: Socratic questioning builds awareness, ownership, and accountability for action.

name: Kolb Experiential Learning Cycle
description: Four-stage learning model: Concrete Experience, Reflective Observation, Abstract Conceptualization, Active Experimentation.
creator: David Kolb
core_principles: Learning emerges from a complete cycle linking experience, reflection, conceptualization, and experimentation.

name: Driscoll Model (What? So What? Now What?)
description: Three-question reflective structure connecting description, significance, and next actions.
creator: John Driscoll
core_principles: Minimal three-step inquiry to extract meaning and define actions from experience.

name: Schön Reflective Practice
description: Dual modes of reflection: Reflection-in-Action during work and Reflection-on-Action after the event.
creator: Donald Schön
core_principles: Practitioners think-in-action and reflect-on-action to adapt and improve professional practice.

name: OSKAR Model
description: Solution-focused coaching model: Outcome, Scaling, Know-how, Affirm and Action, Review.
creator: Paul Z. Jackson and Mark McKergow
core_principles: Focus on resources and preferred future; use scaling and affirmation to build momentum.

name: PDCA Cycle
description: Continuous improvement loop: Plan, Do, Check, Act for iterative change.
creator: W. Edwards Deming
core_principles: Small experiments with feedback and standardization to reduce risk and drive quality.

name: STAR Model
description: Behavioral narration format: Situation, Task, Action, Result to communicate competency.
creator: Behavioral interviewing practice (various)
core_principles: Structured storytelling to evidence capability and outcomes.

name: Decision Matrix
description: Score options against weighted criteria.
creator: Stuart Pugh
core_principles: Define evaluation criteria before scoring options; weight criteria by relative importance; score consistently using defined scale; multiply scores by weights; sum weighted scores to rank objectively; validate top choice against intuition; useful when multiple comparable options exist.

name: Design Thinking
description: User-centered iterative process involving Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, and Test to foster innovation and practical solutions aligned with user needs.
creator: IDEO, Stanford d.school
core_principles: Empathize with users to understand deep needs; define problem statement clearly; ideate without judgment to generate options; prototype rapidly with minimum viable solutions; test with real users and iterate; embrace failure as learning; maintain user-centricity throughout.

name: Agile Retrospectives
description: Structured reflection sessions after sprints or iterations with team members to discuss what worked, what didn’t, and actionable improvements.
creator: Agile Software Development community
core_principles: Create psychological safety for honest feedback; focus on team process not individual performance; identify what worked to sustain good practices; identify what didn't work without blame; generate actionable improvements with clear owners; time-box to maintain focus; conduct immediately after sprint while fresh.

name: Lean Startup Methodology
description: Build-Measure-Learn iterative loop for developing products or services with minimal waste, validated learning, and rapid adaptation.
creator: Eric Ries
core_principles: Build minimum viable product to test assumptions; measure actual user behavior not opinions; learn from data to validate or invalidate hypotheses; pivot or persevere based on evidence; minimize time through build-measure-learn loop; embrace validated learning over vanity metrics; fail fast and cheap.

name: OKR (Objectives and Key Results)
description: Framework to set ambitious, measurable goals with defined Key Results fostering focus, alignment, and accountability.
creator: Andy Grove
core_principles: Set aspirational but achievable objectives; define 3-5 measurable key results per objective; make progress visible and transparent; review regularly (weekly/monthly); maintain focus by limiting concurrent OKRs; accept 60-70% achievement as success; separate OKRs from performance reviews to encourage stretch goals.

name: Liberating Structures
description: Collection of microstructures to facilitate inclusive participation and unleash creativity in groups, e.g., '1-2-4-All,' 'What, So What, Now What?'.
creator: Henri Lipmanowicz, Keith McCandless
core_principles: Include everyone's voice through structured participation; distribute control to unleash local innovation; use simple rules to generate complex outcomes; integrate freedom and constraints; practice to build fluency; adapt structures to context; combine multiple structures for richer engagement.

name: Cynefin Framework
description: Sense-making framework to help leaders decide actions based on categorizing problems into simple, complicated, complex, chaotic, or disorder domains.
creator: Dave Snowden
core_principles: Sense the situation before acting; match response to domain type; Clear domain use best practice; Complicated domain analyze and apply good practice; Complex domain probe-sense-respond with safe-to-fail experiments; Chaotic domain act-sense-respond to stabilize; avoid one-size-fits-all solutions.

name: Remote and Hybrid Team Strategies
description: Frameworks and practices specifically for managing distributed teams, including asynchronous collaboration, virtual whiteboarding, and digital wellbeing methods.
creator: Various contributors
core_principles: Over-communicate to compensate for lack of physical presence; document decisions asynchronously for timezone flexibility; establish explicit working agreements and norms; invest in relationship building intentionally; balance synchronous and asynchronous communication; respect work-life boundaries across timezones; leverage digital tools effectively.

name: 5 Whys
description: Iterative questioning technique asking 'Why?' five times to uncover root causes of a problem.
creator: Taiichi Ohno
core_principles: Ask why iteratively to move beyond symptoms; stop when root cause identified not automatically at five; validate cause-effect logic at each step; avoid blame focus on process; combine with other tools for complex problems; document chain for organizational learning.

name: Eisenhower Matrix
description: Prioritization matrix dividing tasks into urgent/important quadrants to focus effort on what matters most.
creator: Dwight D. Eisenhower
core_principles: Quadrant 1 Urgent/Important do immediately; Quadrant 2 Important/Not Urgent schedule and prioritize; Quadrant 3 Urgent/Not Important delegate or minimize; Quadrant 4 Neither eliminate ruthlessly; invest time in Quadrant 2 to prevent Quadrant 1 fires; distinguish truly urgent from merely reactive.

name: Jobs to be Done
description: Framework focusing on customer 'jobs' (tasks they hire products to do) to drive innovation.
creator: Clayton Christensen
core_principles: Focus on customer outcome not product features; understand job context and constraints; identify emotional and social dimensions of job; recognize jobs are stable while solutions evolve; competition is anything hired for same job; innovate by executing job better than alternatives.

name: MoSCoW Method
description: Prioritization technique categorizing requirements as Must, Should, Could, Won't to manage scope.
creator: Dai Clegg
core_principles: Must Have are non-negotiable requirements for success; Should Have are important but have workarounds; Could Have are nice-to-have if time permits; Won't Have are explicitly out of scope this iteration; revisit categorization as priorities shift; use to manage stakeholder expectations and scope creep.

name: SCAMPER
description: Brainstorming checklist: Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to another use, Eliminate, Reverse to generate ideas.
creator: Bob Eberle
core_principles: Systematically apply each prompt to current solution; Substitute components or materials; Combine with other products or processes; Adapt from other contexts; Modify scale or attributes; Put to another use; Eliminate unnecessary elements; Reverse or rearrange sequence; quantity of ideas leads to quality.

name: Toyota Kata
description: Routine-based practice for improvement: Improvement Kata (scientific experimentation) and Coaching Kata to build habits.
creator: Mike Rother
core_principles: Improvement Kata: understand direction, grasp current condition, establish next target condition, experiment toward target through PDCA cycles; Coaching Kata: develop improvement capability through structured practice; make scientific thinking routine; focus on process not results; coach the thinking not the solution.

name: Double-Loop Learning
description: Learning process where individuals or organizations question and modify underlying assumptions, not just actions, to improve performance.
creator: Chris Argyris
core_principles: Single-loop learning adjusts actions within existing assumptions; double-loop learning questions and modifies underlying assumptions and mental models; surface and test governing variables; distinguish espoused theory from theory-in-use; organizational learning requires changing shared assumptions.

name: Ladder of Inference
description: Framework illustrating how individuals move from observable data to assumptions and conclusions, promoting awareness of cognitive biases.
creator: Chris Argyris
core_principles: Start with observable data; recognize we select data based on beliefs; add meanings based on culture and experience; make assumptions based on meanings; draw conclusions; adopt beliefs about the world; take actions based on beliefs; slow down inference to test assumptions; distinguish observation from interpretation.

name: Balanced Scorecard
description: Strategic management tool that measures organizational performance across financial and non-financial perspectives.
creator: Robert Kaplan and David Norton
core_principles: Balance four perspectives: Financial, Customer, Internal Process, Learning and Growth; connect measures to strategy through cause-effect relationships; lead indicators predict future performance; lag indicators measure past results; cascade scorecard through organization; review regularly to drive strategic execution.

name: Theory of Change
description: Comprehensive framework describing how and why a desired change is expected to happen through a sequence of outcomes and assumptions.
creator: Carol Weiss
core_principles: Map backward from long-term goal through preconditions; make assumptions explicit and testable; identify early and intermediate outcomes; distinguish outputs from outcomes; show causal pathways not just logic; engage stakeholders in theory development; use for planning and evaluation; revise as learning occurs.

name: Appreciative Inquiry
description: Change management approach focusing on identifying and amplifying what works well instead of fixing problems.
creator: David Cooperrider
core_principles: Discover peak experiences when organization at its best; Dream ideal future building on strengths; Design provocative propositions bridging best of past with possibilities; Destiny/Deploy sustain change through ongoing learning and adjustment; focus on positive core strengths not deficits; language shapes reality.

name: Fishbone Diagram
description: Visual tool used to identify root causes of a problem by categorizing potential factors.
creator: Kaoru Ishikawa
core_principles: Organize potential causes into major categories: Methods, Machines, Materials, Measurements, People, Environment; brainstorm causes within each category; trace from symptom to root cause along bones; validate causal relationships with data; useful for complex multi-factor problems; visual format aids team discussion.

name: Mind Mapping
description: Visual technique for organizing information, ideas, and relationships around a central concept.
creator: Tony Buzan
core_principles: Start with central concept in middle; branch out with major themes radiating from center; add sub-branches for details; use colors and images to enhance memory; capture associations non-linearly; mirrors natural thinking patterns; useful for brainstorming, note-taking, and organizing complex information; emphasize relationships over hierarchy.

name: PESTLE Analysis
description: Strategic framework analyzing external factors: Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, and Environmental.
creator: Harvard Business School community
core_principles: Scan external macro-environment systematically; Political factors include regulation and tax policy; Economic factors include growth and exchange rates; Social factors include demographics and culture; Technological factors include innovation and automation; Legal factors include compliance requirements; Environmental factors include sustainability; update regularly as factors evolve.

name: SOAR Analysis
description: Strategic planning framework focusing on Strengths, Opportunities, Aspirations, and Results to drive positive change.
creator: Jacqueline Stavros
core_principles: Strengths focus on what organization does well; Opportunities identify external possibilities; Aspirations articulate inspired future vision; Results define measurable outcomes; positive framing energizes stakeholders; builds on appreciative inquiry principles; contrasts with deficit-focused SWOT; emphasize collaboration over competition.

name: ITIL Incident Management
description: Industry-standard framework for structured incident handling covering Detection, Diagnosis, Repair, Recovery, and Restoration with prioritization matrix based on Impact × Urgency.
creator: UK Government (CCTA)
core_principles: Minimize business impact through rapid restoration; prioritize by urgency and impact; maintain clear communication; document for continuous improvement.

name: Runbook Methodology
description: Pre-documented decision trees and step-by-step procedures for known failure scenarios, encoding expert knowledge for consistent execution.
creator: Operations management practice
core_principles: Standardize responses to known scenarios; reduce mean time to resolution; enable less-experienced staff to execute expert solutions; maintain living documentation.

name: Blameless Post-Mortem
description: Structured analysis of system failures focusing on technical failure chains, timeline reconstruction, contributing factors, and preventive controls without individual blame.
creator: John Allspaw (Etsy)
core_principles: Focus on systems and processes, not people; assume good intent; identify contributing factors holistically; generate actionable preventive measures; psychological safety enables honest analysis.

name: Change Advisory Board (CAB)
description: Governance framework for evaluating change requests through structured risk assessment including blast radius analysis, rollback planning, and approval workflows.
creator: ITIL framework
core_principles: Assess risk before implementation; ensure stakeholder review; validate rollback capability; balance change velocity with stability; document decisions for audit trail.

name: Pre-Mortem Analysis
description: Prospective failure identification technique where team assumes a project has failed spectacularly and works backward to identify potential causes and preventive measures.
creator: Gary Klein
core_principles: Assume failure to overcome optimism bias; surface hidden concerns through safe failure framing; identify preventive actions before commitment; leverage team's tacit knowledge of risks.

name: FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis)
description: Quantitative risk assessment method calculating Risk Priority Number (RPN) as Severity × Occurrence × Detection to prioritize mitigation efforts.
creator: U.S. Military (MIL-P-1629)
core_principles: Systematically identify all potential failure modes; quantify risk through severity, occurrence, and detection scores; prioritize mitigation by RPN; track risk reduction over time.

name: Kano Model
description: Framework categorizing requirements by impact on customer satisfaction: Basic (expected), Performance (linear satisfaction), Delight (unexpected value), Indifferent, and Reverse.
creator: Noriaki Kano
core_principles: Distinguish must-haves from differentiators; invest in delighters for competitive advantage; recognize that features decay from delight to expected over time; balance portfolio across categories.

name: Value vs. Effort Matrix
description: 2×2 prioritization grid plotting initiatives by business value (high/low) against implementation effort (high/low) to identify quick wins and strategic bets.
creator: Management consulting practice
core_principles: Prioritize high-value, low-effort quick wins first; defer low-value work regardless of effort; make strategic bets on high-value, high-effort initiatives intentionally.

name: RICE Scoring
description: Prioritization framework calculating score as (Reach × Impact × Confidence) / Effort to rank features or initiatives objectively.
creator: Intercom (Sean McBride)
core_principles: Use consistent metrics across all initiatives; factor in confidence level to penalize uncertain estimates; normalize by effort to compare fairly; recalibrate periodically based on outcomes.

name: Causal Loop Diagrams
description: Visual modeling tool representing system dynamics through reinforcing and balancing feedback loops to understand non-linear causation and unintended consequences.
creator: Jay Forrester
core_principles: Map relationships, not just components; identify reinforcing loops that amplify change; identify balancing loops that resist change; recognize delays in feedback; anticipate unintended consequences.

name: Theory of Constraints
description: Management methodology identifying and systematically exploiting the single bottleneck limiting system throughput through five focusing steps: Identify, Exploit, Subordinate, Elevate, Repeat.
creator: Eliyahu Goldratt
core_principles: Focus improvement on the constraint; subordinate non-constraints to constraint needs; avoid local optimization that doesn't improve system throughput; constraint shifts after elevation.

name: Wardley Mapping
description: Strategic situational awareness technique visualizing technology components on evolution axis (Genesis → Custom → Product → Commodity) to inform build-vs-buy decisions.
creator: Simon Wardley
core_principles: Map value chain from user needs downward; position components by evolution stage; anticipate component movement toward commodity; exploit inertia and ecosystem positioning.

name: RACI Matrix
description: Responsibility assignment framework defining roles as Responsible (does work), Accountable (decision authority), Consulted (two-way input), Informed (one-way updates).
creator: Management consulting practice
core_principles: One Accountable per task; multiple Responsible allowed; distinguish input-givers (Consulted) from recipients (Informed); clarify decision rights explicitly to reduce conflict.

name: Stakeholder Analysis (Power/Interest Grid)
description: 2×2 matrix categorizing stakeholders by power (high/low) and interest (high/low) to tailor engagement strategy: Manage Closely, Keep Satisfied, Keep Informed, Monitor.
creator: Aubrey Mendelow
core_principles: Allocate engagement effort based on power and interest; manage closely those with both high power and high interest; satisfy high-power low-interest stakeholders; stakeholder positions shift over time.

name: BLUF (Bottom Line Up Front)
description: Communication structure placing conclusion, decision needed, or recommendation in the first sentence, followed by supporting details for time-constrained audiences.
creator: U.S. Military writing practice
core_principles: State the most important information first; respect audience time; enable rapid decision-making; provide supporting detail for those who need it; invert traditional narrative structure.

name: Value Stream Mapping
description: Lean technique visualizing end-to-end process flow with cycle times, wait times, and handoffs to identify non-value-added activities and waste.
creator: Mike Rother and John Shook (Toyota)
core_principles: Map current state before designing future state; distinguish value-added from non-value-added time; identify waste types (waiting, transport, overprocessing); reduce handoffs and batch sizes.

name: Poka-Yoke
description: Error-proofing design principle creating systems that prevent mistakes through constraints, forcing functions, or automatic error detection rather than relying on vigilance.
creator: Shigeo Shingo (Toyota)
core_principles: Design out error possibility rather than detecting errors; use physical or procedural constraints; make errors immediately visible; prefer prevention over inspection.

name: Kanban Method
description: Visual work-in-progress management system limiting concurrent tasks to reduce context-switching, with columns representing workflow stages and explicit WIP limits.
creator: David J. Anderson
core_principles: Visualize work; limit work in progress; manage flow; make policies explicit; implement feedback loops; improve collaboratively through experimentation.

name: After Action Review (AAR)
description: Structured team learning dialogue addressing four questions: What was expected? What actually happened? Why the difference? What will we sustain or improve?
creator: U.S. Army
core_principles: Conduct immediately after event while memory fresh; include all participants regardless of rank; focus on learning not blame; identify both sustains and improves; keep sessions short and focused.

name: Peer Assist
description: Proactive knowledge-seeking workshop where team consults peers with relevant experience before starting significant work to identify risks and leverage lessons learned.
creator: British Petroleum (BP)
core_principles: Seek knowledge before starting not after failing; frame as help request to encourage honest input; focus on learning from similar experiences; apply insights to planning; follow up to share outcomes.

name: Knowledge-Centered Service (KCS)
description: Methodology integrating knowledge creation and reuse into problem-solving workflow through capture during resolution, structuring for reuse, and continuous improvement.
creator: Consortium for Service Innovation
core_principles: Solve and document simultaneously; knowledge is by-product of problem resolution; collective ownership of content; reward knowledge sharing; continuous improvement of articles.

name: Interest-Based Relational (IBR) Approach
description: Conflict resolution method separating people from problems, focusing on underlying interests rather than stated positions, and generating mutual-gain options.
creator: Roger Fisher and William Ury (Harvard)
core_principles: Separate people from problem; focus on interests not positions; generate options for mutual gain; use objective criteria; maintain relationship while solving problem.

name: Crucial Conversations Framework
description: Structured approach for high-stakes, emotional discussions using Start with Heart, Learn to Look, Make it Safe, Master My Stories, STATE (Share facts, Tell story, Ask, Talk tentatively, Encourage testing).
creator: Kerry Patterson, Joseph Grenny, Ron McMillan, Al Switzler
core_principles: Clarify what you really want; watch for safety threats; separate facts from stories; speak persuasively not abrasively; encourage opposing views; move to action with clear commitments.

name: Getting Things Done (GTD)
description: Comprehensive personal workflow management with five steps: Capture (collect everything), Clarify (process meaning), Organize (categorize), Reflect (review), Engage (do).
creator: David Allen
core_principles: Capture everything to free mental RAM; two-minute rule for quick tasks; organize by context and next action; weekly review to maintain system; stress-free productivity through trusted system.

name: Pomodoro Technique
description: Time management method using 25-minute focused work intervals (pomodoros) followed by 5-minute breaks, with longer breaks after four pomodoros to maintain concentration and prevent burnout.
creator: Francesco Cirillo
core_principles: Time-box work into manageable intervals; eliminate distractions during pomodoro; take mandatory breaks to sustain focus; track pomodoros to estimate effort; protect pomodoros from interruptions.

name: Time Blocking
description: Calendar management strategy allocating specific time blocks for different work types (deep work, meetings, email) to prevent reactive context-switching and protect focus time.
creator: Cal Newport (popularized)
core_principles: Proactively schedule deep work before reactive demands fill calendar; batch similar tasks; protect blocks from meeting encroachment; distinguish shallow from deep work; leave buffer time for unexpected.

name: Bloom's Taxonomy
description: Hierarchical classification of learning objectives across six cognitive levels: Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, Create, progressing from lower-order to higher-order thinking.
creator: Benjamin Bloom
core_principles: Build higher-order thinking on lower-order foundation; match assessment to cognitive level; progress systematically through levels; distinguish knowledge types (factual, conceptual, procedural, metacognitive).

name: Scaffolding (Zone of Proximal Development)
description: Instructional technique providing temporary support structures for learners working just beyond their independent capability, gradually reducing assistance as competence increases.
creator: Lev Vygotsky (theory), Jerome Bruner (term)
core_principles: Target zone just beyond independent capability; provide temporary support structures; gradually fade assistance as competence grows; make thinking visible through modeling; transfer responsibility to learner.

name: Socratic Method
description: Teaching through disciplined questioning rather than direct instruction, guiding learners to discover principles and examine assumptions through guided inquiry.
creator: Socrates
core_principles: Question to guide discovery not tell answers; expose contradictions in thinking; probe assumptions systematically; lead learner to self-correct; stimulate critical thinking through dialectic.

name: Threat Modeling
description: Security analysis technique identifying potential threats through frameworks like STRIDE (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, Elevation of Privilege).
creator: Microsoft (Adam Shostack)
core_principles: Model system architecture first; identify assets and trust boundaries; enumerate threats systematically using STRIDE; assess risk and prioritize mitigations; iterate as system evolves.

name: Chaos Engineering
description: Discipline of experimenting on distributed systems to build confidence in capability to withstand turbulent conditions by intentionally injecting failures in production.
creator: Netflix (Jesse Robbins)
core_principles: Build hypothesis about steady-state behavior; introduce real-world failure events; run experiments in production; minimize blast radius; automate experiments; learn from outcomes to improve resilience.

name: Service Level Objectives (SLO)
description: Target reliability metric framework defining acceptable service levels through Service Level Indicators (SLI) and error budgets to balance innovation velocity with stability.
creator: Google SRE (popularized)
core_principles: Define measurable SLIs tied to user experience; set realistic SLO targets below perfect reliability; use error budget to balance risk and velocity; burn budget intentionally for features; freeze changes when budget exhausted.

name: Hypothesis-Driven Development
description: Experimental approach treating features as hypotheses to be validated through measurable outcomes before full implementation, minimizing waste on unvalidated assumptions.
creator: Lean Startup community
core_principles: State assumptions as testable hypotheses; define success metrics upfront; build minimum test to validate; measure actual outcomes; pivot or persevere based on evidence; fail fast on invalid hypotheses.

name: Wardley Doctrine
description: Set of strategic principles derived from gameplay patterns including focus on user needs, use appropriate tools, think small teams, manage inertia, and exploit ecosystems.
creator: Simon Wardley
core_principles: Focus on user needs not technology; use appropriate methods for evolution stage; think small teams with clear ownership; challenge assumptions; exploit ecosystems; manage inertia; effectiveness over efficiency in genesis; efficiency over effectiveness in commodity.
